matchstick.title: Vertical sticks in simple numerals
matchstick.principle: I, II, III, and L consist solely of vertical matchsticks; adding or removing a single vertical stick changes the numeral’s value by exactly one.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral is made only of vertical sticks and you need to increase or decrease its value by one.
matchstick.example: I → II (add a vertical) or III → II (remove a vertical).

matchstick.title: Preserve token validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, both the source character (with a stick removed) and the destination character (with a stick added) must remain valid Roman numerals or allowed operators (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after deciding a stick move, before finalizing it.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' yields '-', which is a valid operator; adding that vertical to an I yields II, also valid.

matchstick.title: Use numeric difference to guide moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of each side of the equation; the difference tells how many units the left side must increase or the right side must decrease (or vice‑versa), guiding which numerals or operators to adjust.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, after parsing the equation.
matchstick.example: If LHS = 3 and RHS = 26, the RHS must be reduced by 23.

matchstick.title: I‑V reordering changes value by 2
matchstick.principle: Moving an I across a V (changing IV to VI or VI to IV) flips the I from subtractive to additive, altering the numeral’s value by exactly two.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains the pattern IV or VI and a vertical stick can be moved across the V.
matchstick.example: IV (4) → VI (6) by moving the I to the right of V.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer between numerals
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick from one numeral to another reduces the source’s value by one and raises the destination’s value by one, provided both remain valid numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust two numerals by opposite one‑unit changes.

matchstick.title: Never take sticks from V or X
matchstick.principle: V and X consist only of diagonal sticks; removing a diagonal would leave an invalid character, so sticks must never be taken from them.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before selecting a source stick, ensure the character is not V or X.
matchstick.example: Do not remove a diagonal from V to create I.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity
matchstick.principle: When moving sticks involving operators, the resulting symbol must still be one of the allowed operators (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is moved from or to an operator.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' yields '-', which is allowed.

matchstick.title: Final verification of equation
matchstick.principle: After performing a stick move, recompute the values of all numerals and verify that the arithmetic holds; if not, backtrack and try a different move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the end of each candidate move.
matchstick.example: After moving a stick, check that III = XV - XII evaluates to true.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick from '+' to numeral
matchstick.principle: Moving the vertical component of a '+' operator to a numeral simultaneously changes '+' to '-' and adds an I (vertical stick) to the numeral, increasing its value by one; this also flips the sign of that term in the arithmetic, turning addition into subtraction.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' and a numeral that can accept an extra I (e.g., ending with I), and you need both to change the operator sign and adjust the numeral’s value.
matchstick.example: III = XV + XI → move vertical from '+' to XI, yielding III = XV - XII.

matchstick.title: Horizontal stick transfer between operators
matchstick.principle: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' (or vice versa) changes '-' to '=', and '=' to '-', preserving operator validity; this can toggle between equality and subtraction signs.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '=' and '-' and you need to switch one of them.
matchstick.example: Turning '-' into '=' by adding a horizontal from '=', or turning '=' into '-' by removing a horizontal.

matchstick.description: Taking a stick from V or X, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: V and X are built only from diagonal sticks; removing one leaves a single diagonal, which is not a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never select a diagonal stick from V or X as a source; only move sticks from characters that contain vertical or horizontal components.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid one
matchstick.why_it_happens: Operators have fixed stick patterns; moving sticks can produce symbols that are not among the allowed operators (+, -, =).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move involving an operator, verify that the resulting symbol is still a valid operator.

matchstick.description: Assuming a single stick can change a numeral's value arbitrarily
matchstick.why_it_happens: Numerals change value in predictable increments (e.g., a vertical stick changes by one, I‑V reordering changes by two); a random stick move may not produce a valid numeral or the expected value change.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Use known value‑change rules for vertical, horizontal, and I‑V moves before deciding on a stick relocation.

matchstick.description: Neglecting to recompute the arithmetic after the move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The puzzle requires the final equation to be numerically correct; forgetting to recalc leads to an invalid solution.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the numeric values of all numerals after a move and check that the equality holds.

matchstick.description: Treating diagonal sticks as interchangeable with vertical sticks
matchstick.why_it_happens: Diagonal sticks belong to V and X and cannot be used as vertical sticks; mixing orientations breaks character validity.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track stick orientation; only move vertical sticks to vertical positions and horizontal sticks to horizontal positions.
